title: .respawnpack/runtime/rollover/<host>-<conversationId>/thresholds.json — which context thresholds have fired THIS CYCLE
description: Written by core/policy/thresholds.js's writeLatches(), and by hooks/context-monitor.js which reads/re-arms/writes this same file directly (not through thresholds.js's own named-threshold latch() helper, because context-monitor.js's advisory/collaborate stages are a caller-defined two-value set — 60/80 — that does not fit the module's fixed advisory/checkpoint/final vocabulary; the module's forCycle/readLatches/writeLatches primitives are host- and caller-agnostic by design and this is exactly the kind of caller they exist for). ⛔ THE WHOLE FILE IS REPLACED, NEVER MERGED, THE MOMENT ITS OWN cycleId NO LONGER MATCHES THE CURRENT ONE — see thresholds.js forCycle(): 'which thresholds already fired' is a fact about ONE context cycle and means nothing in the next, which is the v0.2 defect (a per-SESSION latch that fired once and went silent forever) this file's whole existence corrects. GITIGNORED, machine-local. No schemaVersion: this file is REBUILT EMPTY every time its cycle changes rather than migrated, so there is no format for an old reader to disagree about.

cycleId.description: host:conversationId:cycleIndex:cycleNonce, OR the read-only synthetic 'host:conversationId:0:unestablished' a caller uses before any machine state exists for this conversation — see core/lifecycle/cycle.js.

latched.description: Keyed by threshold name. core/policy/thresholds.js's own latch() only ever writes 'advisory' | 'checkpoint' | 'final'; hooks/context-monitor.js additionally writes its own numeric-string stage keys ('60', '75', '80', '85', ...) for its caller-defined stage arrays, so keys are validated by VALUE SHAPE rather than by a closed name enum.
